_meta.method: Curated from primary sources (press releases, SEC filings, DoD announcements) and trade press (The Robot Report, IEEE Spectrum, TrendForce, Counterpoint, CSIS, Adamas) via seeded web search plus five parallel research sweeps

overview.headline: The U.S. is rebuilding the robot supply chain from both ends — and the middle is missing.
overview.bluf: Capital and federal money now flow into the two ends of the chain: rare-earth magnets (MP Materials, Vulcan, USA Rare Earth — backed by ~$3B+ of DoD equity, loans, and price floors) and final assembly (BotQ, RoboFab, Tesla Fremont, Hyundai's planned 30k/yr Atlas plant). But the precision middle — reducers, roller screws, bearings, frameless motors, dexterous hands — remains roughly 90% Japanese and Chinese, with near-zero U.S. merchant capacity. China controls ~70% of humanoid component supply overall, ~90% of magnet production, and ~89% of lidar; building a U.S. humanoid without Chinese parts roughly triples its bill of materials.

shipments.name: Industrial robots
shipments.definition: Fixed robot arms on production lines — welding, assembly, painting, handling. The biggest robot category by far; includes cobots.
shipments.note: Record level — demand doubled in 10 years. China installed 295,000 (54% of the world); the Americas took ~9%.

shipments.name: Collaborative robots (cobots)
shipments.definition: Robot arms safe to work next to people without cages — a subset of industrial installs. The term for the human-safe niche.
shipments.note: $1.26B market in 2024, heading to $3.4B by 2030; Asia-Pacific holds ~42% of the market.

shipments.name: Professional service robots
shipments.definition: Everything mobile outside the factory cage: AMRs/AGVs in warehouses (~54% of the category), delivery, cleaning, medical, agriculture, hospitality.
shipments.note: +9% YoY; staff shortages are the main demand driver. AMR = autonomous mobile robot (navigates freely); AGV = automated guided vehicle (follows fixed paths).

shipments.name: Humanoids
shipments.definition: Bipedal or wheeled-torso general-purpose robots. The smallest category today and the fastest-growing.
shipments.note: >80% of 2025 installs were in China; 2026 forecast exceeds 50,000 units (+700% YoY).

chain_stages.name: Materials & magnets
chain_stages.note: Rare earths, NdFeB magnets, magnesium — China holds ~90% of refining and magnet output; U.S. capacity is being rebuilt with DoD money but operates at a fraction of announced targets.

chain_stages.name: Precision components
chain_stages.note: Reducers, roller screws, bearings, motors, hands — a Japan–China duopoly with near-zero U.S. merchant capacity. The deepest structural gap in the chain.

chain_stages.name: Sensing & compute
chain_stages.note: U.S. dominates robot-brain design (NVIDIA, Qualcomm) and depth cameras, but lidar is ~89% Chinese and leading-edge chips are fabbed in Taiwan and Korea.

chain_stages.name: Batteries & power
chain_stages.note: Cells follow the EV supply base: Chinese firms hold ~70% of installations. U.S. strength is at the pack/BMS level; no U.S. mass-market robot cell source until ~2028.

chain_stages.name: Final assembly
chain_stages.note: U.S. nameplate capacity now rivals Chinese plans on paper, but realized 2025 output was >80% Chinese. Japanese and European industrial-robot makers are localizing U.S. plants.

chain_stages.name: Deployment & demand
chain_stages.note: Amazon, automakers, and contract manufacturers anchor U.S. demand, while China leads installed base and robot density on factory floors.

categories.name: Rare-earth mining, separation & refining
categories.summary: The U.S. can mine — Mountain Pass produced a record ~50,700 t of REO concentrate in 2025 — but separation and refining is the deepest chokepoint: China held ~91% of global capacity in 2024 and ~99% of heavy rare-earth (Dy/Tb) processing. 2025–26 brought real firsts: Energy Fuels produced the first U.S. primary terbium oxide in decades, Lynas broke China's monopoly on commercial heavy separation (in Malaysia), and ReElement's 16,000 t/yr Indiana refinery starts up in Q3 2026.
categories.share_note: Share of global rare-earth mine output; for separation/refining China's share is ~91%

chokepoints.text: Heavy rare-earth (Dy/Tb) separation was ~99% Chinese as of April 2025; Wuxi hosted the world's only commercial Dy refining in 2025
China's April 2025 export-licensing regime on 7 heavy REEs never lapsed; Dy and Tb exports fell ~50% below pre-restriction levels
Solvent-extraction know-how and trained operators are scarce outside China — and Beijing's Oct 2025 controls also restrict exporting the technology itself
Lynas's DoD-backed Seadrift TX heavy-REE plant is now 'unlikely to proceed' per management, shifting capital to Malaysia

categories.name: NdFeB magnet manufacturing
categories.summary: December 2025 was the inflection point: MP Materials began commercial NdFeB production at Independence (Fort Worth) and e-VAC shipped its first U.S.-made magnets from Sumter, SC. Announced U.S. capacity sums to ~25,000 t/yr by 2028–30 (MP ~10,000, Vulcan 10,000, Noveon 2,000+, USAR 1,200, e-VAC ~1,500) — but mid-2026 operating capacity is only ~3,000–5,000 t/yr against China's ~300,000 t/yr installed base. A humanoid needs ~2–4 kg of NdFeB; one million robots a year would consume more magnet than all current U.S. operating capacity.
categories.share_note: Share of global NdFeB magnet production by volume, 2025

chokepoints.text: Sintering and grain-boundary-diffusion know-how is concentrated in China and Japan; China restricts exporting the process technology
Dy/Tb inputs for high-temperature magnet grades depend on Chinese-licensed exports
Qualification cycles of 12–24 months for automotive and defense customers slow every new entrant
Even at full announced build-out, U.S. capacity is ~10× smaller than China's installed base

categories.name: Specialty structural materials
categories.summary: Robot frames, joint housings, and actuator shells lean on magnesium and aluminum die castings, where China produces ~80% of the world's primary magnesium (1.8M t capacity vs 64,000 t U.S. nameplate). The sole U.S. primary magnesium producer suspended output in 2021–22 and faces permanent shutdown as of late 2025; DoD is seeding alternatives (Magrathea, $19.6M) but domestic primary magnesium is effectively zero today.
categories.share_note: Share of global primary magnesium production

chokepoints.text: No operating U.S. primary magnesium smelter
Die-casting capacity for robot skeletons and housings is overwhelmingly Chinese
2026 U.S. restrictions on Chinese components force OEMs to requalify suppliers against limited Western capacity

categories.name: Actuators & joint modules
categories.summary: Actuators are roughly half a humanoid's bill-of-materials value, and the U.S. position rests almost entirely on OEM vertical integration: Tesla and Figure design and build actuators in-house (Figure has produced 9,000+ at BotQ), but both still depend on Chinese sub-components. Merchant supply at humanoid scale is led by Chinese Tesla-chain firms — Sanhua (reported $685M Optimus order) and Tuopu (~1M units/yr planned in Mexico) — plus Germany's Schaeffler. No U.S. merchant supplier ships actuators in six-figure volumes.
categories.share_note: Approximate merchant humanoid actuator supply capacity announced through mid-2026

chokepoints.text: Tesla's volume actuator orders are concentrated in two Chinese suppliers (Sanhua, Tuopu)
Every actuator motor needs NdFeB magnets — pulling the materials chokepoint into every joint
U.S. in-house lines (Tesla, Figure) are single-customer and can't supply the broader ecosystem

categories.name: Precision reducers (harmonic & cycloidal)
categories.summary: The U.S. has essentially no domestic precision-reducer manufacturing at scale — the category is a Japan–China duopoly. Harmonic Drive Systems (~35% global share) and Nabtesco (~60% of robot cycloidal RV gears) hold the high end; Chinese makers Green Harmonic and Leaderdrive are taking the humanoid volume tier at 30–40% lower prices, with Green Harmonic qualified into Tesla's chain and a 500,000-unit/yr plant entering production in 2026. Harmonic Drive's only U.S. footprint is assembly in Beverly, MA.
categories.share_note: Global harmonic/cycloidal reducer revenue share; 'rest of world' is mostly Japan

chokepoints.text: Strain-wave tooth-grinding know-how sits with HDSI (Japan) and a handful of Suzhou firms
Nabtesco is sole-source-class for large-joint cycloidal RV gears
Zero U.S. domestic strain-wave volume capacity — every robot-grade reducer is imported

categories.name: High-density electric motors
categories.summary: The U.S. retains design leadership in frameless torque motors (Kollmorgen, Moog) and Switzerland in coreless motors (Maxon), but Chinese makers (Leadshine, Johnson Electric, Haozhi) have closed the torque-density gap and dominate volume pricing. The binding constraint is upstream: every high-density robot motor needs NdFeB magnets that China overwhelmingly processes.
categories.share_note: Directional estimate of frameless torque-motor supply for robotics

chokepoints.text: NdFeB magnet dependence — export-license regime since April 2025
Chinese frameless motors now match Western torque density at lower cost, eroding the pricing umbrella

categories.name: Roller screws, ball screws & bearings
categories.summary: High-end ball screws are ~90% Japanese/German (THK, NSK, Rexroth) and planetary roller screws ~80% European (Rollvis, GSA, Ewellix) — but China is scaling fastest for humanoid volume: Hengli's ball-screw lines entered production in Nov 2025 inside Tesla's chain, and Xinjian broke ground on a 1M-unit/yr roller-screw base. Each Optimus uses ~14 roller screws and 14–20 crossed-roller bearings, making this the most supply-constrained linear-motion segment. U.S. production is negligible (SKF's Kaydon thin-section plant in Muskegon, MI is the main domestic site).
categories.share_note: Directional share of robot-grade screws and precision bearings; 'rest of world' is mostly Japan, Switzerland, Germany

chokepoints.text: Precision thread grinding to <5 µm tolerance concentrated in Rollvis and Nippon Thompson, both near capacity
Optimus roller-screw lead times hit 26 weeks in 2023; raw-material delays add 12–18 weeks
The thread-grinding machine tools themselves are Japanese/Swiss/German
Crossed-roller bearing grinding sits with 3–4 Japanese and German firms

categories.name: Dexterous hands & end effectors
categories.summary: China has run away with volume: Beijing's Linkerbot claims >80% of the global high-DoF dexterous hand market, shipped its 10,000th hand in Nov 2025, raised $150M, and is targeting a ~$6B-valuation Hong Kong IPO. The Western position (Shadow Robot, Psyonic, Wonik Allegro) is research-grade and low volume. Tesla keeps Optimus hands in-house — ~50 actuators across both hands — and Musk says the hand consumes over half of total Optimus engineering effort.
categories.share_note: Global high-DoF dexterous hand unit share

chokepoints.text: Linkerbot is the only mass producer above 1,000 high-DoF hands/month — single-company concentration
Micro coreless motors and micro screws for fingers come largely from Swiss and Chinese micro-motor makers
Hands are the engineering bottleneck for entire humanoids — Musk says over half of Optimus engineering effort

categories.name: Sensors (force/torque, tactile, vision, lidar)
categories.summary: The U.S. holds genuine strength in six-axis force/torque sensing (ATI, Apex NC), tactile (GelSight), and depth cameras (RealSense — embedded in ~60% of the world's AMRs and humanoids) — but has effectively lost lidar: Chinese suppliers hold ~89% of the global market, RoboSense's robotics-lidar shipments grew 1,459% YoY in Q1 2026, and Luminar filed Chapter 11 in Dec 2025, leaving Ouster as the main U.S. merchant player. China is also scaling six-axis F/T sensor output at 50%+ annual growth.
categories.share_note: China share is lidar-specific (Yole Group, 2025); the U.S. leads in F/T, tactile and depth cameras

chokepoints.text: Lidar: four Chinese firms hold ~89% of the global market; Western alternatives are shrinking
Six-axis F/T calibration capacity — each unit is individually calibrated; U.S. capacity was sized for industrial robots, not million-unit humanoid volumes
RealSense alone is in ~60% of AMRs/humanoids — a single-vendor dependency, though a U.S. one
Tactile/e-skin remains pre-industrial, funded at SBIR scale rather than volume capex

categories.name: Compute & semiconductors
categories.summary: The U.S. dominates robot-brain design: NVIDIA's Jetson Thor (Blackwell, 2,070 FP4 TFLOPS, 128 GB) is the de facto humanoid compute standard — adopted by Agility, Boston Dynamics, Figure, Amazon, and Meta — with Qualcomm's 700-TOPS Dragonwing IQ10 and Ambarella as U.S.-designed alternatives. The structural weakness is manufacturing: every leading robot SoC is fabbed at TSMC (Taiwan) or Samsung (Korea), though TSMC Arizona produced its first U.S.-made Blackwell wafer in Oct 2025.
categories.share_note: No published share series; U.S. firms dominate design, Taiwan/Korea dominate fabrication

chokepoints.text: Jetson Thor's silicon is built on TSMC's custom 4N/4NP process — U.S.-designed, Taiwan-fabbed
128 GB LPDDR5X memory per Thor module comes from Korean memory makers
Robot foundation-model training competes for the same NVIDIA data-center GPU pool as LLM training

categories.name: Batteries & power systems
categories.summary: Humanoid packs are small (~0.9–2.3 kWh), so cell volume is modest — but supply mirrors the EV market, where Chinese makers held ~70% of 2025 global installations (CATL 39%, BYD 16%). The U.S. is competitive at the pack/BMS level — Figure builds its 2.3 kWh F.03 structural pack in-house at BotQ — and in premium silicon-anode cells (Amprius), but EnerSys's DOE-backed $615M South Carolina gigafactory won't produce until 2028. Korean makers (LGES, Samsung SDI) are positioning as the non-Chinese cell source for Optimus-class robots.
categories.share_note: Chinese firms' share of global EV/lithium cell installations in 2025 — the supply base robot cells draw from

chokepoints.text: Over 55% of global cells come from two Chinese firms (CATL + BYD)
No U.S. mass-market robot-grade cell source until EnerSys Greenville starts in 2028
First-of-kind safety certification (UN38.3 + UL2271) capacity for humanoid batteries is scarce
High-discharge sub-2.5 kWh form factors are a contested Korean niche (4680 cells, future solid-state)

categories.name: Robot final assembly & integration
categories.summary: Final assembly is the most visible U.S. push: BotQ ramped from one robot/day to one per hour in four months, Tesla is converting Fremont's Model S/X lines for late-2026 Optimus mass production, Agility's RoboFab is designed for 10,000 Digits/yr, and Hyundai plans 30,000 Atlas robots/yr near its Savannah Metaplant by 2028. But realized output is still overwhelmingly Chinese — China took >80% of the ~16,000 humanoid installations in 2025, AgiBot hit its 10,000th cumulative unit in March 2026, and Unitree targets 20,000 units this year. In industrial robots, FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, and Universal Robots are all localizing U.S. assembly.

facts.label: China component-chain control
facts.value: ~70% of the global humanoid component supply chain (motors, actuators, sensors, batteries, materials)

facts.label: BOM without Chinese suppliers
facts.value: Building Optimus Gen 2 without Chinese suppliers raises BOM from ~$46K to ~$131K (~3×)

facts.label: NdFeB per humanoid
facts.value: ~2–4 kg per robot — roughly 2–3× an EV's magnet content; 1M robots/yr ≈ 3,500 t/yr, more than current U.S. operating magnet capacity

facts.label: China separation/refining share
facts.value: ~91% of global rare-earth separation capacity (2024); ~99% of heavy-REE processing as of April 2025

facts.label: Export-control impact
facts.value: Dy and Tb exports fell ~50% below pre-restriction levels; U.S. yttrium imports from China fell from 333 t to 17 t

facts.label: US magnet outlook
facts.value: Adamas: U.S. briefly reaches magnet demand parity ~2028, before robotics/AI demand outruns supply again

facts.label: 2025 humanoid installations
facts.value: ~16,000 units globally; China >80%; AgiBot No. 1 at ~31%

facts.label: 2026 humanoid forecast
facts.value: >50,000 units globally (+700% YoY); China output +94%; Unitree + AgiBot ~80% of China share

facts.label: Actuator share of BOM
facts.value: Actuators are ~50% of humanoid bill-of-materials value (Schaeffler)

facts.label: Roller screws per Optimus
facts.value: ~14 planetary roller screws per robot; lead times hit 26 weeks in 2023

facts.label: 2025 robotics VC
facts.value: ~$14B per Crunchbase (vs $8.2B in 2024); broader trackers report $35–40B including megadeals

facts.label: 2026 YTD robotics VC
facts.value: $23B+ globally by mid-2026, nearly matching all of 2025; Q1 humanoid equity funding $2.37B (+288% YoY)

facts.label: DFARS magnet deadline
facts.value: January 2027 deadline for non-China magnet sourcing in defense systems; China's Oct 2025 export-control expansion suspended only until Nov 2026
